parsed.headline: Israeli settlers attack European diplomats and officials in West Bank

pages.text: Masked Israeli settlers attacked a convoy of European diplomats and officials in the occupied West Bank on Saturday, according to reports from Arab News and The Guardian World. The incident occurred near the village of Taybeh, where a delegation including the French consul general in Jerusalem, the Belgian consul, and the Polish consul were participating in an olive harvest on lands belonging to the Christian town. Witnesses reported that a group of seven men, some armed with clubs, arrived on all-terrain vehicles, surrounded the convoy, and demanded identification documents. During the confrontation, a window of an armored car belonging to the Belgian mission was smashed, and three people were injured. Bernard Baudoux, the mayor of the French town Aulnoye-Aymeries, was reportedly assaulted and knocked to the ground while attempting to enter a vehicle with diplomatic plates. The group also allegedly threatened Baudoux’s wife and Vincent Dollmann, the archbishop of Cambrai. One witness stated a masked militant shouted “Vive la France” during the attack. Belgian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Maxime Prévot condemned the violence, stating that the country would continue to push for European Union sanctions on settlers. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot demanded that Israeli authorities arrest those responsible and halt the violence. The Israeli military condemned the attack as a severe act of violence and stated that police had opened an investigation, noting that the delegation’s tour had not been coordinated with Israeli forces and no soldiers were present at the scene. Meanwhile, the office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu suggested the reports might be part of a coordinated campaign to smear Israel and its residents during the annual olive harvest.

The assault on diplomats followed a separate incident on Friday in which Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine was injured by Israeli settlers near the village of Abu Falah, northeast of Ramallah. Levine, who was wearing a press vest and helmet, reported being pushed to the ground and kicked by a group of settlers while photographing Palestinian farmers harvesting olives. According to The Guardian World and NPR World, the attack lasted more than 10 minutes and resulted in the theft of her passport, phone, wallet, and equipment. Levine was treated at a hospital in Ramallah. The Washington Post denounced the attack and called for a thorough investigation. Palestinian authorities reported that attacks in eight villages resulted in injuries to at least 20 people. The Israeli Foreign Press Association stated that such attacks against journalists and civilians have occurred repeatedly, despite calls for action. The United Nations noted that recent levels of settler violence during the harvest season have reached an all-time high.

parsed.headline: Bangladesh reports 202,000 suspected measles cases during outbreak

pages.text: Bangladesh is managing a measles outbreak that has resulted in 202,000 suspected cases, including 22,000 laboratory-confirmed instances, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). The WHO reported these figures for the period spanning from the start of the outbreak in mid-March through October 9. The number of suspected cases in Bangladesh is higher than any other country this year. The WHO stated that 1,147 people have died from the disease, with 94 percent of those deaths occurring among children under five years old. Experts note that the country's routine vaccination coverage dropped in 2025, falling below the 95 percent threshold the WHO identifies as necessary to prevent outbreaks. Mark Jit, a WHO vaccine adviser and professor at the School of Global Public Health at New York University, described the situation as a real warning to other nations regarding the risks of declining immunization rates. A Reuters review of WHO documents and interviews with health officials and scientists indicated the emergency response was hampered by shortcomings in preparation, inadequate outreach to parents, and data that omitted millions of children.

In September, Ziauddin Hyder, the special assistant on health affairs to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, told Reuters that the government was doing everything possible to end the outbreak. The government did not respond to further questions sent in October.

parsed.headline: President Mahama advises Ghana's CSIR to commercialize research findings to drive industrialization

pages.text: President John Dramani Mahama has urged the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) in Ghana to translate research findings into commercially viable innovations to drive industrialization, create jobs, and improve livelihoods. In a speech read on his behalf by Dr. Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, Minister of Environment, Science and Technology, the President stated that science, technology, and innovation must be central to the country's economic transformation to enable the development of local technologies and the processing of raw materials into higher-value products. The remarks were made during the opening of the three-day CSIR Innovation Fair 2026 in Accra on October 16, 2026. The fair, which runs from October 16 to 18, brought together 13 CSIR research institutes from across the country to exhibit products, technologies, and services. Dr. Agyeman-Rawlings officially opened the event at the Efua Sutherland Children’s Park in Accra. Under the theme “From Research to Market: The Role of CSIR in Driving Innovation for National Development,” the fair aims to connect researchers, innovators, start-ups, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), industry players, investors, policymakers, and the public. President Mahama noted that the CSIR has established a foundation of expertise in fields including agriculture, food processing, biotechnology, forestry, water resources, construction, renewable energy, and environmental management, but stressed the necessity of translating that knowledge into economic and social benefits. He identified research and innovation as critical to the success of the 24-Hour Economy and the Accelerated Export Development Programme. To support these goals, the President urged the CSIR to deepen collaborations with industry, the 24-Hour Economy Authority, financial institutions, and private investors to identify sectors where research can accelerate production, industrialization, and export growth.

parsed.headline: Zelenskyy describes U.S. pause on Russia sanctions as a reward for Putin

pages.text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has described U.S. President Donald Trump’s decision to pause a package of restrictions targeting the Russian economy as a “reward” for Vladimir Putin. Speaking on Saturday, Zelenskyy warned that the move could embolden the Russian leader and intensify the Kremlin’s war. He expressed expectation that the Trump administration will lift further sanctions against Russia in the future, identifying a “diesel deal” as a first step in that process. While Zelenskyy did not directly criticize the U.S. leader in a social media statement, he described the decision as unfortunate and stated that it disregarded the Lindsey Graham Act, which was intended to impose effective pressure on Russia to end the war. Zelenskyy called for Europe to establish its own negotiations with Moscow as the U.S. seeks better ties and business deals with the Kremlin. He noted that the decision to block the legislation could encourage Russia to continue its military actions without bringing the war to an end.

parsed.headline: Yemeni military claims 1,417 strikes against Houthi targets in 24-hour period

pages.text: Yemen’s armed forces stated on Saturday that they conducted 1,417 strikes against Iran-backed Houthi targets over a 24-hour period, according to a military spokesperson. The spokesperson claimed the operations, part of Operation Dawn of Yemen, resulted in approximately 800 fighters being killed or wounded and more than 190 military vehicles and other assets being destroyed or disabled. According to Arab News, the military spokesperson said the strikes utilized combat aircraft, drones, field artillery, and rocket launchers to target Houthi gatherings, reinforcements, fortified positions, firing points, armored vehicles, combat equipment, and drone launch sites. The spokesperson added that the operations disrupted Houthi movements and prevented the group from sending reserves to front lines or achieving tactical objectives. On the eastern front, Yemeni forces reportedly continued to sweep Houthi positions and expand controlled areas, establishing control over a new tactical position. In Taiz, the armed forces and the Popular Resistance said they repelled successive waves of attacks while combat aircraft struck Houthi positions and reinforcements. The military spokesperson stated that operations were restricted to legitimate military targets and conducted in accordance with international humanitarian law and customary rules. Additionally, the armed forces issued an appeal to residents in Houthi-controlled areas to protect their sons from recruitment campaigns, warning against sending them to fight in battles they claimed do not represent Yemeni national interests.
